statistical_region_merging — SEGMENTATION graph op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.statistical_region_merging(image, *, q: 'float' = 32.0, g: 'int' = 256, value_range=(0.0, 1.0), connectivity: 'int' = 4) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import seggraph; seggraph.statistical_region_merging(image, *, q: 'float' = 32.0, g: 'int' = 256, value_range=(0.0, 1.0), connectivity: 'int' = 4) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("statistical_region_merging"))

Usage

Statistical region merging SRM (Nock–Nielsen 2004): processes pairs of neighbouring pixels in ascending order of |I_p − I_q| and merges them when the predicate P(R, R') holds (statistical_region_merging).

Pixel values are used after mapping value_range linearly onto [0, g − 1] (values outside the range give ValueError). P(R, R') ⇔ |R̄ − R̄'| ≤ √(b²(R) + b²(R')), b(R) = g √(ln(|R_|R||/δ) / (2Q|R|)), ln|R_l| = min(l, g) ln(l + 1), δ = 1/(6|I|²) (the coefficients of the predicate are to be verified, see the module description). The larger Q (q), the smaller b and the more reluctant the merging (finer).

Returns: labels (1..k), n_regions, means (mean per region, on the original value scale), n_merges, q.
